evals.prompt: Design an Event-Driven Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Security Remediation Pipeline for `HIGH` and `CRITICAL` Security Hub findings (`Security Hub Findings - Imported`). Provide: (1) the Amazon EventBridge event pattern JSON, (2) the AWS Step Functions Amazon States Language (ASL) state machine using `sns:publish.waitForTaskToken` with a 24-hour (`86400`s) timeout, post-remediation verification, and automatic rollback on failure, and (3) how the approval callback works.
evals.expected_output: Provides the EventBridge ASFF filter rule, the Step Functions ASL JSON with `arn:aws:states:::sns:publish.waitForTaskToken` (`$$.Task.Token`), `TimeoutSeconds: 86400`, `VerifyRemediationState`, and `ExecuteRollback`, and explains `SendTaskSuccess` / `SendTaskFailure`.
expectations: Provides the EventBridge rule matching `source: ["aws.securityhub"]`, `detail-type: ["Security Hub Findings - Imported"]`, `Compliance.Status: ["FAILED"]`, `Workflow.Status: ["NEW"]`, `RecordState: ["ACTIVE"]`, and `Severity.Label: ["HIGH", "CRITICAL"]`

Provides the Step Functions ASL state machine using `Resource: "arn:aws:states:::sns:publish.waitForTaskToken"` passing `"TaskToken.$": "$$.Task.Token"` and `TimeoutSeconds: 86400` (routing `States.Timeout` to an `ApprovalTimedOut` state)
Includes a `VerifyRemediationState` step after `ExecuteAtomicRemediation` that routes to `ExecuteRollback` (`Catch` / `VerificationPassed == false`) if verification fails
Explains that the human approver clicks a signed approval link (API Gateway / Lambda / ChatOps) that invokes `states:SendTaskSuccess` (or `states:SendTaskFailure` to reject) with the `TaskToken`

evals.prompt: Before our remediation workflow revokes `0.0.0.0/0` ingress on port `5432` from Security Group `sg-0abc123456def7890` and tightens the Key Policy on KMS CMK `arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:187382368021:key/11112222-3333-4444-5555-666677778888`, what exact read-only Phase 1 Active-Usage Pre-Flight checks must be executed to prevent dropping live database traffic or causing an irreversible KMS key lockout? Include the exact verification and rollback commands.
evals.expected_output: Details the mandatory read-only pre-flight checks for Security Groups (`ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces --filters Name=group-id` + VPC Flow Logs active connection check) and KMS CMKs (`kms:GetKeyPolicy` + `kms:ListGrants` + CloudTrail caller check + preserving the `arn:aws:iam::187382368021:root` admin statement), along with verification and rollback commands.
expectations: For the Security Group: requires calling `ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces` (`--filters Name=group-id,Values=sg-0abc123456def7890`) to identify all attached ENIs/RDS/EC2 instances AND querying VPC Flow Logs on those ENIs to identify legitimate source CIDRs/Security Groups before revoking `0.0.0.0/0`
For the KMS Key Policy: requires calling `kms:GetKeyPolicy` and `kms:ListGrants` and checking CloudTrail `Decrypt`/`GenerateDataKey` callers before modifying the policy
Emphasizes that the KMS Key Policy update MUST preserve the account root administrative statement (`arn:aws:iam::187382368021:root`) so the CMK never becomes permanently unmanageable

Provides exact post-remediation verification commands (`ec2 describe-security-groups`, `kms get-key-policy`) and deterministic rollback commands (`ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress`, `kms put-key-policy --policy file://backup-key-policy.json`)

evals.prompt: We want a governed remediation plan for two findings in our live `ap-south-1` (`client-devops`) account: (1) IAM user `sandeep.mahto`'s active access key `AKIASXIG4A4KWCDEMHZF` is >90 days old, and (2) S3 bucket `krayak-dev-8021-as1-terraform-tfstate` has `BucketKeyEnabled: false` and needs an explicit KMS key enforcement statement merged into its existing bucket policy. expectations: Invokes read-only MCP tools (`iam` and/or `aws-mcp`) in `ap-south-1` to inspect `AKIASXIG4A4KWCDEMHZF` (`GetAccessKeyLastUsed` / `iam_evaluate_access_keys`) and `krayak-dev-8021-as1-terraform-tfstate` (`GetBucketPolicy`, `GetBucketEncryption`) without running raw `aws` CLI in `Bash`

Proposes deactivating the IAM access key first (`update-access-key --status Inactive`) after provisioning/rotating a replacement rather than immediately running `delete-access-key`

Formats the output according to the 5-part Standardized Remediation Proposal Contract (`Target Resource & Finding Summary`, `Blast-Radius & Active-Usage Pre-Flight Report`, `Proposed Remediation Payload` with `approval_required: true`, `Post-Remediation Verification Check`, and `Deterministic Rollback Procedure`)

Invokes `awsiac` MCP (`validate_cloudformation_template` and/or `check_cloudformation_template_compliance`) to validate the CloudFormation template

evals.prompt: Our platform team uses both AWS CDK (TypeScript) and Terraform 1.10+. Show how to implement shift-left governance in both tools: (1) how to wire `cdk-nag` `AwsSolutionsChecks` into a CDK app and why `NagSuppressions.addResourceSuppressionsByPath` must be used instead of `addStackSuppressions`, and (2) how to configure an `aws_db_instance` in Terraform 1.10+ using `ephemeral` resources and write-only (`password_wo`) attributes (or `manage_master_user_password`) so plaintext database passwords never enter `terraform.tfstate`.
evals.expected_output: Provides the TypeScript `cdk-nag` `AwsSolutionsChecks` + `NagSuppressions.addResourceSuppressionsByPath` code and the Terraform 1.10+ `ephemeral "random_password"` + `password_wo` / `password_wo_version` + `manage_master_user_password = true` HCL configuration.
expectations: Shows `Aspects.of(app).add(new AwsSolutionsChecks({ verbose: true }))` in TypeScript CDK and explains that `NagSuppressions.addStackSuppressions` is forbidden because it masks violations across all resources in the stack, requiring `NagSuppressions.addResourceSuppressionsByPath` with a specific reason (`>= 10` characters referencing an approved security exception/ticket)

Shows the Terraform 1.10+ `ephemeral "random_password"` block paired with `password_wo = ephemeral.random_password.db_master.result` and `password_wo_version` on `aws_db_instance` (and/or `manage_master_user_password = true` with `master_user_secret_kms_key_id`)
Explains that `ephemeral` values and `_wo` (write-only) attributes are sent to the AWS API during `apply` but are never written to `terraform.tfstate` or plan files

evals.prompt: Execute Workflow A (Architectural Threat Modeling) for our multi-account financial platform: an internet-facing API Gateway and ALB (`TB-1`) route traffic to ECS Fargate tasks in private subnets (`TB-2`) that assume IAM roles (`TB-3`) across a Data Lake account in our AWS Organization (`TB-4`) and invoke an Amazon Bedrock Agent with MCP tools (`TB-5`). Map the 5 Trust Boundaries, trace 2 multi-service attack paths (`Initial Access -> Credential Access -> Lateral Movement -> Exfiltration`), and produce a Prioritized Threat Matrix (`P0`–`P3`) mapped to Preventive, Detective, and Responsive controls.
evals.expected_output: Maps all 5 Trust Boundaries (`TB-1` through `TB-5`), traces 2 multi-service attack paths across compute/IAM/data, and outputs a `P0`–`P3` Prioritized Threat Matrix with Preventive, Detective, and Responsive AWS controls.
expectations: Defines all 5 Trust Boundaries: `TB-1` (Internet/Edge), `TB-2` (VPC/Subnet/Security Group), `TB-3` (IAM/STS Identity Boundary), `TB-4` (Multi-Account/Organization Data Perimeter), and `TB-5` (GenAI/Agentic Execution Boundary)

Traces at least 2 multi-service attack paths end-to-end (`Initial Access -> Credential Access -> Lateral Movement -> Data Exfiltration`, such as SSRF/container compromise -> task role theft -> cross-account S3 exfiltration, and indirect prompt injection in Bedrock -> MCP tool invocation -> unauthorized mutation)

Produces a Prioritized Threat Matrix (`P0` Critical to `P3` Low) mapping each threat to Preventive (WAFv2, SG chaining, `aws:PrincipalOrgID`/`aws:SourceVpc`, `aws:ViaAWSMCPService`), Detective (GuardDuty, CloudTrail Data/Network Activity events, Security Hub), and Responsive (EventBridge + Step Functions HITL containment) controls
